name: Luana Santos
event: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan
summary: A 27-year-old Brazilian grappler (11-2; 6-1 UFC) who moved up from flyweight and has won three straight at bantamweight. Most recently she shut out Karol Rosa 30-27 on all three cards with more than 12 minutes of control. She has never been finished, and calls herself a 'suffocating' fighter.

how_they_fight.Striking: Low volume (about 2.4 significant strikes a minute) but efficient and hard to hit. Mainly a leg kick and a sharp 1-2 to enter, plus overhand rights on the way to the clinch (Cageside, on Croden and Rosa). Has one TKO in the UFC (Juliana Miller, R1).
how_they_fight.Grappling: The core of her game: judo, takedowns in open space and against the fence, long top control (51% control share), back takes. Kept Rosa down for 741 seconds and Croden for 561 seconds. Five submissions, including an Americana of Tainara Lisboa at 4:59 of R2 and an R1 finish of Mariya Agapova.
how_they_fight.Defense: Very good: 70% striking defense, absorbs only 1.6 a minute, 77% takedown defense. Never stopped. Both losses were decisions (a split to Jena Bishop in LFA, and Casey O'Neill out-landing her 83-41 at UFC 305).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Steady three-round grinder. Six finishes: four in R1 (three submissions plus the Miller TKO), one at 4:59 of R2 (Lisboa) and one early in R3 (regional, 2022). Her last two fights went the distance with control in every round, so she doesn't fade. Has never been stopped in any round.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Patient and disciplined: picks her entries, then stays heavy on top. She loses when out-worked at range by a volume striker who stays upright (O'Neill).

patterns: Takedown, then long top control and back takes
Low-volume, efficient striking to set up entries
Never finished; both losses were decisions
Finishes come early (four of six in R1) or not at all; her last two wins were 15-minute grinds
concerns: Out-landed badly by a high-volume striker (O'Neill 83-41)
Low striking output means she can drop rounds where she doesn't get the takedown
Smaller frame than a natural bantamweight
keys_to_beat: Keep her at range and out-volume her
Defend the first takedown and make her strike

news.text: Beat Karol Rosa by unanimous decision (30-27 x3), controlling most of the fight.
Said her goal is to be UFC champion in 2027 and called herself a fighter who can suffocate anyone in the division (Cageside).
Rankings disagree: Cageside lists her at No. 3; the UFC.com event page shows the pair at No. 6 and No. 7.
